known.title: Not done: Close refuses the skip after a blocking review, and tests, CI, the design checks and the merge step still run on a skipped item.

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done.
Case: normal use - continuing a shared item after merging remote review history into a locally advanced branch.
This call uses review._history, whose traversal follows only first parents (src/forge/review.py:596). If the remote branch contains a blocked round followed by a clean round, merging it into a stale clone with local work puts those rounds behind the merge's second parent. The first-parent traversal sees the latest clean snapshot but misses the earlier block, so --no-review is accepted. close_remote.reconcile also creates this merge shape at src/forge/close_remote.py:56; checking again after reconciliation does not recover the omitted rounds. The permanent refusal must inspect the item's review history across merged parents. The current stale-clone test only exercises a fast-forward.
findings.title: Not done: Close refuses the skip after a blocking review, and tests, CI, the design checks and the merge step still run on a skipped item.

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 1
Raise: Test.
Case: normal use - GitHub requires merging an updated default branch while a skipped close waits for CI.
The unchanged-diff case never exercises the retry it claims to prove. Its helper adds only NEWS.md on main, and the inherited PR-list stub supplies no BEHIND status (tests/test_close.py:285). For that conflict-free change, _merge_default returns without merging at src/forge/close.py:753-755, leaving HEAD unchanged and avoiding the recursive close. These assertions therefore pass even if a base-only retry loses the saved skip and unnecessarily runs a model review. Make this case require the default-branch merge and verify its ancestry before asserting that the skip survives.
